title: Peak latency report overstates one endpoint
summary: The per-endpoint peak latency report shows one endpoint far slower than its own traces support, and a latency regression review is stuck on the discrepancy.
task: Report each endpoint's slowest request latency in milliseconds and how many requests it saw, so the performance reviewer can sign off on the latency regression.

company.notes: Observability latency rollup; subtle accumulator-scope flaw, no syntax error.

expected_output:
=== Peak latency by endpoint ===
/login: peak=200ms over 2
/search: peak=60ms over 3
/checkout: peak=900ms over 2
buggy_output:
=== Peak latency by endpoint ===
/login: peak=200ms over 2
/search: peak=200ms over 3
/checkout: peak=900ms over 2

phase2.spec_patch: Ops now also meters 'internal' service-to-service calls, not just external requests. Fold internal calls into each endpoint's peak latency and request count the same way.
phase2.expected_output_v2:
=== Peak latency by endpoint ===
/login: peak=200ms over 2
/search: peak=500ms over 4
/checkout: peak=900ms over 3
